old_title: Hayden Panettiere latest: On-off boyfriend ends silence before late actor's birthday
new_title: Hayden Panettiere's boyfriend was there when she died. Their history is complicated
old_text:
Hayden Panettiere, who became a household name as a teenager for her role in Heroes and later starred in Nashville and multiple Scream films, has died at age 36.
Panettiere was pronounced dead at a South Carolina apartment Sunday, August 16. A cause of death has not been revealed, but an autopsy showed no signs of trauma. Toxicology reports are pending and could take up to 12 weeks, according to the Greenville County Coroner's Office.
An investigation is reportedly being conducted into Panettiere's death involving Greenville police as well as the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration after an incident report stated that her on-off boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, turned over a "bag of medication" to police.
On Thursday (20 August), the day before Panettiere's 37th birthday, his lawyer told TMZ: "Hayden's death remains under investigation and it is important to allow that investigation to proceed. As has been publicly reported, police confirmed there were no signs of foul play."
Panettiere was best-known for playing Sheryl Yoast in the 2000 Denzel Washington-led film Remember the Titans, high school cheerleader Claire Bennet on NBC's sci-fi drama Heroes (2006-2010), and aspiring country singer Juliette Barnes on the hit TV series Nashville (2012-2018).
Her New York Times bestselling memoir, This Is Me: A Reckoning, was published in May this year, in which she looked back at her childhood in Hollywood and her experiences with addiction, postpartum depression (which she claimed cost her a sponsorship with skincare brand Neutrogena), abusive relationships, and the loss of custody of her daughter, Kaya, whom she shares with former heavyweight boxer Wladimir Klitschko.
Hayden Panettiere's on-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson breaks silence
Brian Hickerson has broken his silence following Hayden Panettiere's death, issuing his first statement through his lawyer, Sloan Ellis.
"Hayden's death remains under investigation and it is important to allow that investigation to proceed," Ellis said in a statement to TMZ. "As has been publicly reported, police confirmed there were no signs of foul play."
The statement added: "Out of respect for Hayden's loved ones and the ongoing investigation, there will be no further comment at this time."
Hickerson, who had an on-and-off relationship with Panettiere, was at the apartment when Panettiere was found unresponsive on Sunday, along with his brother Zach. He showed responding officers a bag of medication Panettiere had been taking, while authorities later said an autopsy found no signs of trauma.
The DEA has since joined the investigation, and Panettiere's cause and manner of death remain pending.
Hickerson also has a history of domestic violence against Panettiere and pleaded no contest to two felony charges involving her in 2021.
'Bursting with brilliance': Hayden Panettiere remembered by her biggest co-stars
Hayden Panettiere has been remembered by actors she worked with throughout her career.
Connie Britton, who played Rayna Jaymes opposite Panettiere's Juliette Barnes on Nashville, shared photos of the pair and wrote: "This was Hayden. Bursting with brilliance, shining so bright. I have no words for this sad song. Just heartbreak. I love you girl. Sleep easy now."
Esten recalled meeting Panettiere when he auditioned for Nashville, remembering how she listened outside the audition room before surprising him with a smile and telling him: "That was so good!!"
Jack Coleman, who played Claire Bennet's father on Heroes, remembered Panettiere as a "prodigious talent" and said: "She was a tiny colossus who loved to laugh." Masi Oka, who played Hiro Nakamura, described her as possessing a "beautiful spirit" and "immense talent".
Cattrall, who played Panettiere's mother in Ice Princess, wrote simply: "Rest in peace sweet Hayden. Gone far too soon."
Viola Davis, who worked with Panettiere on The Architect and Custody, remembered her as "an old, wise soul with such a deep heart".
Hayden Panettiere said fame could 'turn your life upside down' in 2007 interview
Hayden Panettiere spoke about the pressures facing young women in Hollywood and the relentless attention of the paparazzi when she was just 18.
Asked about the years since Heroes had made her famous, Panettiere told GQ in 2007: "This business tends to turn your life upside down. For some strange reason, I've become one of the targets of the paparazzi. Things get crazy. You try and hold on to that little part of normal that you can."
On whether the media was effectively pushing young women towards public meltdowns, she pointed to Britney Spears, who was facing intense scrutiny at the time, saying: "That girl was the epitome of beauty when I was younger. And we built her up and just ripped her down, put every aspect of her life under a microscope."
She added: "Probably made 90 per cent of the stuff up along the way. I can't even imagine if I had it like she does. She's someone that I'm rooting for, and I hope she can make that comeback."
Panettiere's Heroes co-star Jack Coleman recently recalled the intense scrutiny she faced as a teenager, saying in his tribute to her that she had been "hunted" by paparazzi.
"They were predatory," Coleman wrote. "No one, especially a teenager, should be targeted that way."
Neutrogena breaks silence after backlash
Panettiere's death prompted the actor's previous comments about how she was "fired" from being the face of the brand for speaking out about her postpartum depression to resurface.
"We are deeply saddened by Hayden Panettiere's passing," the company said in a statement posted to its social media accounts. "For more than a decade, Hayden was a valued member of our Neutrogena community."
"We are proud to have partnered with her and understand that we made her feel unsupported during a very difficult time. This is not what Neutrogena stands for or who we want to be," the statement continued.
Hayden Panettiere said she was focused on 'finding meaning in life' months before her death
Hayden Panettiere spoke about finding purpose in her life and looking towards new creative opportunities just months before her death.
"I know that if I surround myself with positive people, I can accomplish whatever I set my mind to," she told The Independent in May, and said she wanted to write and produce, and release a jewellery line.
"I've made my share of mistakes, I've fallen on my face, but I've always stood up again and dusted myself off."
She added: "I've got plenty of issues, but finding meaning in life isn't one of them."
Panettiere said creativity had provided a "lifeline" and given her purpose when she needed it most.
Hayden Panettiere would have celebrated her 37th birthday today
Hayden Panettiere would have turned 37 today, just five days after the actor died suddenly at the age of 36.
Panettiere was born on 21 August 1989 and died on 16 August in South Carolina. She was said to have been looking forward to spending her birthday with her 11-year-old daughter, Kaya, in Germany.
A source close to the actor told Page Six that she had been "so excited to see her" and had been telling people how much she was looking forward to spending time with her daughter.
Panettiere's memoir This Is Me: A Reckoning was published in May, in which she wrote openly about her childhood in Hollywood, addiction, postpartum depression, abusive relationships, and the loss of custody of Kaya.
The heartbreaking family struggles that shaped Hayden Panettiere's life off screen
The 'Heroes' and 'Nashville' star, who has tragically died aged 36, was bracingly honest about her experiences of familial estrangement, losing custody of her daughter and the depression that followed the sudden death of her younger brother, writes Katie Rosseinsky
Hayden Panettiere was a passionate advocate of Ukraine
Panettiere's daughter moved to Ukraine to live with her father, boxer Wladimir Klitschko, in 2018, when Russia had illegally annexed Crimea in 2014 and separatist forces were fighting Ukrainian troops in the Donbas region.
When Vladimir Putin launched his full-scale invasion in February 2022, Klitschko, whose brother Vitalii is the mayor of Kyiv and also a former boxing champion, enlisted in the army. Kaya, the outlet reported, was not in Ukraine from the early days of the war.
Panettiere posted repeated messages of solidarity with Ukraine on Instagram in the years that followed.
"I have personally witnessed the strength of the Ukrainian people who fought so hard for their independence and have continued to passionately defend their country over the years. What Putin is doing is an absolute disgrace!," she wrote on Instagram shortly after the invasion.
"This horrific moment in history sends a terrifying message: the message that in this day and age, in year 2022, it's okay to violate the rights of free people and allow autocrats like Putin to take whatever they please," she added.
'We made her feel unsupported': Neutrogena responds after Hayden Panettiere's death
Neutrogena has addressed criticism over its treatment of Hayden Panettiere, saying it understands that the actor felt "unsupported" during a difficult period in her life.
The skincare brand said in a statement on Thursday: "We are deeply saddened by Hayden Panettiere's passing. For more than a decade, Hayden was a valued member of our Neutrogena community."
"We are proud to have partnered with her and understand that we made her feel unsupported during a very difficult time," it continued. "This is not what Neutrogena stands for or who we want to be."
Neutrogena vowed to make a "significant investment to a long-standing community health partner" to support women's health causes and promised to share more details "when plans are in place."
Panettiere wrote in her memoir that Neutrogena cancelled her long-standing contract in 2015 after she spoke publicly about her postpartum depression. In a May interview with Jay Shetty, she said: "Of all the things that they would fire me over, this is the last thing that I thought they would ever fire me for."
new_text:
When Hayden Panettiere died this Sunday, the 36-year-old Heroes and Nashville star was in South Carolina with an on-and-off boyfriend she'd once described as her "abuser."
Panettiere first started dating Brian Hickerson, an aspiring actor and real estate agent, in 2018. At the time, she had recently broken up with heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko, who is the father of her daughter, Kaya.
In the early days of their courtship, Panettiere and Hickerson were photographed by paparazzi in Los Angeles attending film screenings and eating brunch with friends.
However, by the following year their relationship had taken a dark turn. On May 2, 2019, according to Los Angeles County criminal court records, Hickerson was arrested on allegations of injuring a spouse or girlfriend. The alleged incident occurred at their home after a night of drinking, and Hickerson was subsequently ordered not to contact Panettiere and to stay at least 100 yards away from her.
That case was eventually dismissed, and the couple reunited only for another alleged violent incident to occur in Wyoming on Valentine's Day 2020, when Hickerson was arrested once again. Later that year, prosecutors in Los Angeles charged him with four counts of injuring a spouse or cohabitant, two counts of assault with a deadly weapon, one count of dissuading a witness and one misdemeanor battery count, all linked to alleged incidents involving Panettiere between 2019 and 2020.
In July 2020, Panettiere spoke out about the way she had been treated. In a statement posted on Twitter (now X), she shared the number for a domestic abuse hotline online and wrote: "I am coming forward with the truth about what happened to me with the hope that my story will empower others in abusive relationships to get the help they need and deserve. I am prepared to do my part to make sure this man never hurts anyone again."
Less than a year later, in April 2021, Hickerson pleaded no contest to two felony counts of injuring a spouse or girlfriend and was sentenced to 45 days in jail, four years of probation and 52 domestic violence classes.
However, the couple later rekindled their relationship once again. In April 2023, in the write-up of an interview with the New York Times, a journalist noted that Hickerson was "walking around, vacuuming and shooting a basketball through the hoop in her living area" during their meeting.
Panettiere admitted at the time that "there are feelings" between the pair, and that Hickerson had got sober and their relationship was "contingent on him continuing on this road of recovery."
She added: "He knows he deserved what happened to him. I did not do any of this lightly."
In May 2026, Panettiere, who was open about her own struggles with opioid addiction, published her memoir This Is Me: A Reckoning and reflected further on what her relationship with Hickerson had put her through.
She wrote that she never wanted to become a "spokesperson for domestic violence," adding: "I never wanted to call myself a victim, but here I am. It's part of my story whether I want it to be or not."
In the book, Panettiere wrote that Hickerson beat her so badly on one occasion that she did not leave the house for weeks, and that she hesitated to report the alleged abuse to police out of concern that the public would find out.
When Panettiere was interviewed by The Independent that month, she said she was single. Her representatives stated that she and Hickerson were no longer in contact with one another, despite being photographed together a couple of months prior.
When Panettiere's mother, Lesley Vogel, heard about her daughter's death, she thought of Hickerson immediately. "This person in her life that we have been trying to get rid of for quite some time was with her at her death and that was Brian Hickerson," she told NBC News.
According to a police incident report, Brian and his brother Zach Hickerson called 911 when Panettiere was dying. Officers recorded that Zach was emotional as emergency services worked to save Panettiere's life, but that Brian only became emotional after she was officially declared dead. The report also stated that Brian turned over a "bag of medication" belonging to Panettiere to investigators.
A cause of death has not been revealed, but an autopsy showed no signs of trauma.
In June, Panettiere shared a journal entry she had written reflecting on their relationship on Jay Shetty's On Purpose podcast.
"I realized that I was more afraid of being alone than being abused," she said. "In order to be around that behavior, it took me dulling my senses and numbing myself with substances in order to silence that rational voice in my head that was telling me exactly what was going on, and the many reasons why I needed to get myself out of this toxic relationship and as far away from this person as possible."
Rape Crisis offers support for those affected by rape and sexual abuse. You can call them on 0808 802 9999 in England and Wales, 0808 801 0302 in Scotland, and 0800 0246 991 in Northern Ireland, or visit their website at www.rapecrisis.org.uk. If you are in the US, you can call Rainn on 800-656-HOPE (4673)
